newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AVH spurts higher after Pride deal.
newsitem.headline: AVH spurts higher after Pride deal.

text.p: Shares in Ackermans & van Haaren (AVH) opened more than three percent higher on Tuesday after news late on Monday that the Belgian holding company stood to make a capital gain of some 1.0 billion francs on a share swap involving one of its units.
The stock was up 180 francs, or 3.7 percent, at 5,020 at 0915 GMT after opening at 5,000 francs.
AVH's Forasol-Foramer NV unit is to merge with Pride Petroleum Services Inc, a Houston-based provider of contract drilling and plugging and abandonment services.
Both companies are Nasdaq-listed. After the news Forasol shares closed $2 higher at 15-7/8 in New York, Pride was up $5/8 at 15-7/8.
Under the deal Forasol shareholders can swap one Forasol share for 0.66 Pride share plus $6.80 in cash.
AVH, whose shares were suspended on the Brussels bourse on Monday pending the news, will receive about 1.07 billion francs in cash plus a 7.2 percent stake in Pride.
At Monday's closing prices Forasol stock is worth $17.28 under the terms of the deal.
One analyst noted every $1 gain by Forasol stock should translate into a 50 franc increase in AVH shares.

He said that even after the merger of Forasol and Pride, AVH would remain invested in a sector heading for an upswing. Forasol should break even in 1996 before posting a $1-$1.1 per share profit in 1997.
"Many players have not discounted that yet, maybe they will once they look at the share again," he added.
